rule: Anonymous subclass instantiation (`new Iface() {…}`, ...): no constructor edge when the named type is an interface/trait (it has no constructor); when it is a class (including abstract), `Type#<init>`, constructor, as usual. Calls inside the body fold into the enclosing function as before. ... Anonymous functions, lambdas, object-literal methods and anonymous-class members fold into the nearest enclosing named function
notes: call_type convention (SPEC names the six call_types but does not define direct vs method): a call with no written receiver is direct; a call with a written receiver (obj., this., super., a type name) is method; new/super(...)/this(...) are constructor. Line 7 `new Listener() {..}`: Listener is an interface, no constructor edge. Line 13 `new Job("x") {..}`: Job is an abstract class, Job#<init>. The anonymous members on/exec and the lambda `n -> handle(n)` fold into Bus#wire. `handle` inside them is a bare call to Bus's member (no such member on Listener/Job). `l` is declared Listener and `j` declared Job: Listener#on and Job#exec are body-less declarations of scanned types, high (Decisions 2026-11-09). `@Override` is not a call.
